head: 332b399af5968c5bdfe909013af69cf25a579e19
classification_reasons: Blast radius is wide even though the spec is tight: check_ratchets is wired into CHECKS_BY_PHASE['c'/'d'/'e'], affecting every project the plugin runs on, plus new helpers in plugin/gate/diff.py, an extension of plugin/state/unpark.py's risk_hits (shared with the pre-existing risk_list acceptance path) and a new clause in plugin/pr/description.py's _conformance_line -- all code every change in every project will now execute at three gates.

This is new deterministic gate behavior with no prior-cycle test coverage: every behavior (two pure drop rules, the --name-status -M parser, tree_files, the declaration/acceptance paths, the skip-marker scan) is exercised only by the roughly 25 tests this same diff adds, not by pre-existing coverage.

spec.md's flagged concerns are all closed and its acceptance criteria are concrete and already matched one-for-one by named tests in plan.md's Proof list, which argues for tightness, but the first criterion (small blast radius) fails, so routine's three-part bar is not met.
attempted: Intent: walked intent.md's 'Proposed outcome' bullet by bullet against the diff. Every bullet is implemented: the ratchets check at (c)/(d)/(e) only (test_checks_by_phase_ratchets_membership); the test-file drop rule (D, or R out of test_paths) in dropped_test_files; the eval-case drop rule (dot-renamed destination, or no survivor left in tree_files(ctx.diff.head)) in dropped_eval_cases; declaration via plan.md's Files-that-change or a '- ratchet: <name> may fall, because <why>' Proof line read at the merge base only (ctx.approved_artifact, never the working tree); the undeclared-drop hit keyed 'ratchet: tests'/'ratchet: evals', accepted by status.yaml: risk_accepted with no new label (unpark.py's RISK_HIT_CHECKS union); the 15-token skip-marker scan (verified the token tuple against intent.md's own list, line by line -- identical, in order); the adversarial-reviewer's new angle 7 and template/REVIEW.md's new bullet; the plugin version bump (1.0.1 -> 1.0.2 in both manifests). Nothing solves a problem adjacent to the stated one; this is the stated one.

Spec and plan: cross-read every Requirements bullet of spec.md against plugin/gate/checks.py and plugin/gate/diff.py directly (not the author's description) -- check_ratchets's structure, the hits/declared/skip_markers detail shape, the `_declared_ratchets` regex anchored on 'ratchet: (tests|evals)', and the eval-case 'probe' trick that appends '.' to a directory path so plan_sync.is_planned's directory-prefix branch matches a folder-level drop -- all match spec.md's Design section's own description, including the riskiest-step mitigation (test_ratchets_plan_edited_after_merge_base_does_not_excuse_drop, which commits the plan.md declaration only on the branch and confirms the drop still fails). Confirmed every file plan.md's 'Files that change' names appears in the diff and no extra production file does; the diff's own file ordering is git's alphabetical default, not plan.md's prose order, which is expected and not a deviation. Confirmed the plan.md edit in this diff (splitting the combined plugin.json/marketplace.json bullet) is explained by and consistent with a real bug the build session found and fixed (art.planned_files only reads a list item's first backtick span), not an undisclosed scope change.

Proof: the verifier.md in evidence/ is a genuine second, fresh-context pass (distinct from the build session's own fix-response.md round 3 claims) and is honest about its limits: it directly executed the diff parser, both pure drop-rule functions, and eleven check_ratchets scenarios against a disposable git fixture, but explicitly did not execute unpark.risk_hits's union behavior, _conformance_line's declared-drops clause, or the risk_list-vs-ratchet separate-hit-key test live, naming those three as 'untested by me, confirmed only by reading the implementation.' I closed that gap myself by reading the three pieces of source directly rather than trusting either the verifier's or the build session's narrative: plugin/state/unpark.py's RISK_HIT_CHECKS=('risk_list','ratchets') and its set-union loop, plugin/pr/description.py's _conformance_line appending the declared-drops clause, and check_risk_list's separate 'tests' (bare) vs check_ratchets's 'ratchet: tests' key -- all three read correctly against their respective tests' expectations. The only full-suite 'commands' result committed in evidence/gate-c.json (1664 passed) is timestamped 2026-10-15T16:04:27Z, before fix-response.md round 3 (collected 16:11:03) added the actual ratchets implementation -- so that record is stale for this HEAD and I did not cite it for or against the change, per instructions; the session's own disclosed sandbox limitation (the sample-python-project .env fixture permission denial) is transparently reported, not hidden, and the deterministic commands/build/lint check will re-run for real on this HEAD regardless of my verdict.

Blast radius: confirmed no sdlc.yaml risk_list item, auth, data migration, money movement or production-config path is touched (spec.md's own 'Does not apply' section and my own read of the diff agree); confirmed no guardrail file (CLAUDE.md, .claude/**, this repo's own root REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) is edited -- template/REVIEW.md is template content the plugin ships, which intent.md's 'Framework change: yes' licenses this run to touch, and the root REVIEW.md edit is correctly only proposed via docs/PROGRESS.md's table, never written. Confirmed check_ratchets's own CHECKS_BY_PHASE wiring is additive (no existing check's signature or call site changes) and that unpark.risk_hits's other caller (plugin/state/cli.py accept-risk) gets the wider union for free with no code change of its own, matching plan.md's Risks section.

Policies: security-baseline's no-shell-string rule -- checked that the new git invocations (diff.py's name_status, tree_files, and checks.py's skip_marker_hits) all go through the module's existing _git/argument-list helper, never a formatted shell string. data-conventions N/A confirmed (no new stored field or migration; the dropped-path/skip-marker details are source-tree metadata already in git history). No third-party dependency added.

Tests: read the actual implementation to check whether the new tests could pass with a latent bug still present, rather than trust the test names. Traced dropped_eval_cases's set logic by hand against all four of its own test scenarios (full case drop, dot-rename, partial multi-file delete with surviving sibling, internal move) and confirmed the survivor-vs-touched-vs-dot-dropped set arithmetic produces the expected result in each case, not just a test that happens to pass by accident. Found one real but non-blocking defect: in tests/test_templates.py, the diff inserts the new `test_review_md_skip_marker_rule_present` function in the middle of the pre-existing `test_review_md_structure` function body (no blank-line boundary before the trailing '# rules added by the guide' comment and its .claude/** / plan.md assertions), so those three pre-existing assertions are now attributed to the new, differently-named test instead of the one whose name describes them. This is a nit (style/attribution, not a behavior, security or policy break): both sets of assertions still execute and still pass under pytest's function discovery; no coverage is lost, only mislabeled, which I note for the author but do not treat as an Important finding under REVIEW.md's bar.

Noted but deliberately not used as a reason: the deterministic 'commands' check (build/test/lint) will re-run on this exact HEAD after this verdict and is the authoritative judge of whether the full suite is green; I did not re-run it and did not cite the stale committed gate-c.json record for or against the change.
